A1.justification: Both complete, readable 18-page PDFs describe the same ExMesh work and include the supplementary material. Text and rendered-page comparison establish that differences are confined to title capitalization and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and rendering experiments on DTU and NeRF-synthetic, alongside ablations and supplementary efficiency results (Tables 1–5 and 7; Figures 8–14).

after.justification: v2 retains the original DTU and NeRF-synthetic experiments, ablations, and supplementary efficiency results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 7 retain identical vertex splitting and merging procedures, geometry/texture optimization, UV maintenance, loss functions, and pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 15 DTU objects and eight NeRF-synthetic scenes, with unchanged reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, and initialization test coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each comparison in Tables 1–3 and 7 and the qualitative figures. The baseline descriptions in Sections 4.2 and 8.2 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, image resolutions, masking rules, initialization, training schedules, and evaluation metrics remain identical in Sections 4 and 8. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3 and 10 retain the same topology, initialization, texture representation, UV reconstruction, hyperparameter, and loss ablations, together with the face-count analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative comparisons are identical, including the supplementary results. For example, ExMesh's mean Chamfer Distance remains 0.58 on DTU in Table 1 and 0.64 on NeRF-synthetic in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(10), including splitting scores, degeneracy criteria, and loss formulations, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about direct explicit mesh optimization, adaptive topology updates, real-time UV maintenance, and the balance of accuracy, efficiency, and mesh conciseness.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the rendering gap relative to Gaussian methods, sensitivity to initialization, hyperparameter tuning requirements, and the CPU-based UV-unwrapping scalability bottleneck in Section 11.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including PyTorch/CUDA/nvdiffrast usage, RTX 3090 hardware, initialization instructions, supplementary pseudocode, and Table 6 hyperparameters. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The same 61 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against implicit, Gaussian-based, and mesh-driven approaches, including the novelty claims, is unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes 'EXplicit' to 'Explicit' on the main and supplementary title pages. The arXiv stamp updates from v1 dated 5 June 2026 to v2 dated 31 August 2026. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The only visual differences are the title and version/date text edits described under P1.

improvement.justification: v2 standardizes title capitalization and updates the version/date stamp. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and supplementary material are unchanged, so these cosmetic edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
